stories.title: Saudi Arabia denies WSJ report claiming Houthis demanded $51bn to halt hostilities
summary: Saudi Arabia has denied a report by the US-based Wall Street Journal (WSJ) that Yemen’s Houthis had demanded $51 billion from kingdom in return for a “negotiated halt” to the ongoing hostilities between the two sides.
The WSJ report and the Saudi denial has come amid renewed hostilities between Riyadh and the Houthis, linked to the larger Middle East conflict.
Then in July, the Houthis triggered a return to hostilities in Yemen when they let an Iranian plane land in defiance of Saudi control of Yemeni airspace.

stories.title: Maliha Ali takes bronze at MMA worlds as Pakistan appeals semi-final decision
summary: When Omar Ahmed, president of the Pakistan MMA Federation, asked if she could compete, her response was simple. “Sir, we fight from the heart,” she said. “These hands and feet are just not that important.” That courage carried her to the semi-final.

Maliha’s run at the IMMAF World Championships in Tbilisi, Georgia, ended in a bronze medal and a dispute on Thursday, with the Pakistan MMA Federation filing a formal appeal over her split-decision loss to Russia’s Polina Baldina in the featherweight (65.8kg) semi-final.
Baldina, 23, is a former world champion in a different MMA federation, having won a world title in Khanty-Mansiysk in 2024, and had won three bouts en route to the final.

stories.title: The Democrats' historic duty
summary: While anger at Trump was the main variable shaping the election’s outcome, the Democrats benefited from the high quality of their candidates in most key races.
If Congressional Democrats bow to Big Tech, they will soon find themselves back where they were two years ago.
US voters have dealt Trump a sharp rebuke, which Democrats—indeed, all Americans—should celebrate.

stories.title: PTI expresses concern over Imran's health, urges CJP to ensure court orders on treatment are implemented
summary: ISLAMABAD: The PTI’s core committee has expressed concern over jailed party founder Imran Khan’s health, urging the chief justice of Pakistan to ensure the effective implementation of court orders regarding the ex-prime minister’s treatment.

A statement issued after the meeting said the committee had expressed “grave concern” over Imran’s health, citing the alleged lack of medical facilities and obstacles to his access to family members and personal physicians.

On Aug 18, the Supreme Court directed the government to shift the jailed ex-premier to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad, a day after the superintendent of the Adiala jail — where Imran is imprisoned — submitted a report to the SC on the ex-premier’s health condition.

stories.title: UN Security Council adopts Pakistan-led statement urging diplomacy during wars
summary: The Pakistani initiative builds on Security Council Resolution 2788, unanimously adopted during Pakistan’s presidency of the Council in July 2025, which reaffirmed the importance of a peaceful settlement of international disputes under the UN Charter.
It encouraged them to continue using mediation, good offices and diplomatic engagement to reduce tensions and facilitate transitions from confrontation to peaceful resolution.
It encouraged the secretary-general to continue supporting diplomatic efforts before and during armed conflicts, including initiatives aimed at de-escalation and sustainable political solutions.

stories.title: Eight killed, 30 injured in bus-truck collision on Hazara Motorway
summary: ABBOTABAD: At least eight people were killed and 30 others injured when a passenger bus collided with a dumper truck near the Havelian Interchange on the Hazara Motorway early Friday morning, rescue officials said.
A day earlier, a collision between a passenger bus and truck claimed the lives of 11 people and left 33 others injured near Pakpattan.
Last week, at least five people were killed and 27 others injured when a passenger bus plunged into a drain in Punjab’s Hafizabad district.

stories.title: Game Review — I love and loathe the mixed bag that is Modern Warfare 4
summary: While gunplay improved massively, the maps were solid, and it felt like a good CoD game again, these were offset by a very, very badly implemented skill-based matchmaking (SBMM) system, “innovations” with little practical benefit, and poor network code and lag issues.
There are even bits where you take control of North Korean soldiers to flesh out the game’s world, albeit reinforcing the stereotype.

Multiplayer: Fun, but frustrating This is the component I’ve spent the most time with so far, and it’s largely standard fare when it comes to CoD: fast, reflex-driven action on small maps with two teams of six.

stories.title: Official rates of beef and mutton increased by Rs50-100 per kg in Karachi
summary: According to new rates notified by the Karachi commissioner, the new official rates of beef, with and without bones, are fixed at Rs1,050 and Rs1,350, respectively, up by Rs50 per kg compared to the rates announced in February.
The official veal rates, with and without bones, have been raised to Rs1,350 and Rs1,650, showing a rise of Rs50 per kg.
As per weekly data of the Sensitive Price Index (SPI), mutton rates in Karachi have already risen to Rs2,200-3,000 per kg in the last one and a half months, compared to Rs2,000-2,800 per kg.

stories.title: Asia stocks tumble after AI rout rocks US markets
summary: A rout in Asia’s tech-heavy markets deepened on Friday as fear of increased regulatory scrutiny and a slowdown in AI build-out precipitated the steepest decline in US stocks since the tariff-triggered “Liberation Day” selloff in April 2025.
Japan’s Nikkei slumped 7 per cent immediately after the opening bell while benchmark share price indices in South Korea and Taiwan dropped more than 8pc.
Kioxia plunged 14pc in Japan while TSMC fell as much 8.5pc in Taiwan.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court declares levy of excise duty on hand-stemmed tobacco illegal
summary: PESHAWAR: Peshawar High Court has declared that Federal Excise Duty (FED) couldn’t be imposed on green leaf and hand-stemmed tobacco unless it has been processed and converted by a green leaf threshing (GLT) unit.

The bench also set aside show-cause notices and orders issued to the petitioners to the extent that they sought to impose FED on hand-stemmed, stemmed or green leaf tobacco not processed through a GLT unit.
The bench observed that the levy in question was tied to the conversion of tobacco green leaf into unmanufactured tobacco through processing by a GLT unit.

stories.title: Man kills niece for ‘honour’ in KP's Oghi
summary: MANSEHRA: A man from the Kohistan region has allegedly killed his 18-year-old niece and injured a man and his cousin in an honour-related incident in Oghi. “The suspect first shot dead his niece at home and then went outside and opened fire on her alleged paramour and his cousin.
Police arrested the suspect after booking him under sections 302 and 311 of the Pakistan Penal Code.

The two were taken to the tehsil headquarters hospital in Oghi where doctors declared the condition of one of them critical. “We have arrested the suspected killer,” Oghi police station SHO Amir Khan said.

stories.title: 98 women get bail after 273 arrested by NCCIA in raid on ‘illegal’ call centre in Karachi
summary: On Nov 4, the NCCIA had raided an office premises in connection with an ongoing enquiry into an alleged international financial fraud network and arrested as many as 273 suspects, including women, in a case pertaining to the theft of credit card data through “spoofed calls”.
The officer also informed the court that he required physical custody of only nine suspects, including the owners, while the remaining suspects should be sent to prison on judicial remand.

After hearing the arguments and examining aspects of the case, the court granted bail to 98 female suspects and juvenile male suspects, subject to verification of their ages through National Database and Registration Authority records, against surety bonds of Rs5,000 each.

stories.title: Two policemen held in ‘gang rape’ case in GB's Rahimabad
summary: SWAT: The Rahimabad police on Thursday arrested two suspects, both serving police constables, in connection with the alleged gang rape of a woman who had travelled to Swat from Peshawar.
Taking immediate notice of the complaint, Swat DPO Umar Khan directed police to arrest the suspects.
When contacted, DPO Swat Umar Khan confirmed that both suspects were serving police constables.

stories.title: Move to legalise sheesha lounges in Islamabad opposed
summary: The meeting highlighted the growing tension between public health imperatives and commercial pressures from the hospitality industry and sheesha interest groups.

However, public health advocates have raised the alarm that the Minister for Health (representing Mr Sattar’s political party) is reportedly considering granting permissions for sheesha establishments in Islamabad.
During the meeting, the team detailed the severe public health consequences of sheesha consumption, particularly its devastating impact on youth and children.

stories.title: Police to introduce e-ticketing at bus stands in Rawalpindi
summary: RAWALPINDI: Police have decided to introduce e-ticketing at bus stands to maintain a digital record of passengers through the Travel Eye app.

The police will also gather the record of passengers staying in hotels, guest houses and inns through the Hotel Eye app ahead of the upcoming ICC Test championship series scheduled to be held in Rawalpindi from Nov 9 to 13.
The SSP said that it had been decided to start special police surveillance at bus/wagon stands and to establish a police post inside the general bus stand as part of the foolproof security.

stories.title: Hyderabad's Nara Jail-SITE land dispute remains unsettled despite ‘agreement’ on papers
summary: The jail administration insists that functioning industries and industrial plots form part of the prison’s land — a claim the SITE management strongly contests.

The SITE management says that the matter had become a ‘closed transaction’ in view of a 12-year-old memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the two government entities on the very land, as well as the past demarcations done on the jail administration’s requests.
The dispute arose in October 2025 when the jail administration started construction of a boundary wall and the SITE management raised objection and claimed ownership of the land.

stories.title: PM opens Kashmir Chowk Underpass in Islamabad, calls its completion in 27 days a ‘mini miracle’
summary: CDA workers give final touches to the newly constructed Kashmir Chowk Underpass site in Islamabad before its inauguration on Thursday. — APP ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday inaugurated Kashmir Chowk Underpass, which was completed in a record 27 days.

Says project was required before next year’s SCO conference in Islamabad He said that the speedy completion of the underpass showed that other initiatives related to the SCO conference will also be completed in the shortest possible time.

During the construction work, the interior minister and CDA Chairman Sohail Ashraf visited the site many times to push Habib Construction Service and CDA teams for its early completion and finally the project was completed in 27 days.

summary: LAHORE: Punjab Commerce and Investment Minister Shafay Hussain of the PML-Q has said that he is standing by his younger brother Salik Hussain, Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis, come what may.
In response to the ongoing controversy involving Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz and Salik Hussain, Mr Shafay said: “I have and will never distance myself from my younger brother.
Shafay Hussain has rejected Salik’s allegations,” Ms Bokhari said responding to Dawn’s queries.

stories.title: Punjab CM directs DCs to highlight govt initiatives at colleges, varsities
summary: The PML-N government, particularly Ms Maryam, has been focusing on engaging students and projecting its performance through visits to educational institutions in Punjab.
The PML-N, particularly Maryam Nawaz, is therefore making a concerted effort to win them over by highlighting the government’s performance,” a PML-N senior leader told Dawn.
Meanwhile, the chief minister also directed DCs to prepare a “District Economic Plan” aimed at promoting economic activity and harnessing the development potential of their respective areas.

stories.title: Melania Trump hosts Russia-Ukraine meeting, calls for ‘enduring’ truce
summary: WASHINGTON: US First Lady Melania Trump called for a “more enduring” ceasefire in Ukraine as she hosted a rare meeting between officials from the war-torn country and its invader Russia at the White House on Thursday.

Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev said he thanked Melania Trump on Put­in’s behalf for her “distinguished humanitarian role” in brokering the truce in Oleshky and for work on reuniting children separated from their families by the war.
The US first lady’s efforts come ahead of trilateral talks next week in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the Ukraine war — the first between Russia, Ukraine and the United States since February.

stories.title: PSX drops around 1,500 points by midday
summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) suspended trading at midday on Friday for the regular Friday prayers break, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index down 1,494.09 points, or 0.85 per cent, at 173,885.77.
By the time of the break, it stood well below the previous close of 175,379.86.
The market is expected to resume after the prayers break and will continue until the regular close.

stories.title: Rule of the people?
summary: A useful analogy is that of Brazil, where Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva recently staved off the most recent articulation of Bolsanarismo — the parallel ideology to Trumpism — to win his fourth term as president.
But the far right under the leadership of the Bolsanaro family also has a mobilised social base, which will rebound from the election loss.
Lula is 81, and his Workers Party will have to deepen the social struggle to keep Bolsanarismo at bay in the years to come.

stories.title: NADRA assistant director shot dead near office in Peshawar
summary: On Tuesday, two policemen were martyred, and another was injured when unidentified armed men attacked a polio vaccination team in K-P's Mohmand district.

Earlier in the week, four polio workers were abducted by unidentified armed men after being subjected to gunfire in K-P's Tank district, while two other members of a polio vaccination team, who had been kidnapped in Lower South Waziristan, were subsequently released.
In a separate incident, two members of a polio vaccination team were abducted by armed men in the Azam Warsak area of Lower South Waziristan.

stories.title: AJK Election Commission imposes curbs in seven Poonch, Sudhnoti constituencies
summary: No candidate or their supporter will be allowed to inaugurate any development project, while government employees, other than those assigned security duties, have been barred from attending election-related public gatherings or participating in candidates’ campaigns.
The commission directed government employees to maintain political neutrality and refrain from using their official influence to support or oppose any candidate or participate in election campaigns.

The commission also called upon the AJK government and law enforcement agencies to take necessary measures to improve the law and order situation in the affected constituencies so that elections could be held at the earliest and public unease over the delay could be addressed.

summary: The incentives and structure of the economy resemble anything but a viable plan for sustained improvement in living standards and chances of shared prosperity.

Since at least the time of Adam Smith’s seminal work (1776), it has been understood that it is the most valuable input in the process of economic growth, something that Paul Romer’s endogenous growth theory (1990) put an authoritative stamp upon.
His current research focuses on the long-term analysis of various issues plaguing Pakistan’s economy, as well as economic reforms and the history of economic thought.

summary: Washington’s interest in Pakistan’s crypto and minerals sectors is largely seen as a by-product of the American president’s close ties with the country’s rulers.

But as the White House’s internal and external dealings come under greater scrutiny when a Democrat-led Congress starts business in January, Pakistan should be prepared for attitudes to change — and not necessarily for the better.
However, even with the Democrats controlling Congress, Pakistan-US ties do not have to nosedive.

stories.title: Governor Kundi insists emergency in KP imposed under extraordinary circumstances
summary: He added that all political parties would be taken into confidence to steer the province towards peace, stability and development, expressing confidence that terrorism would soon be eliminated.

Mr Kundi paid tribute to KP journalists for their sacrifices during the war against terrorism and said effective measures were being taken to address their financial difficulties, ensure their protection and resolve their professional issues.
He said practical measures were being taken to promote tourism, while efforts were underway to award mineral contracts to local companies on a priority basis and attract international investors.

stories.title: Hamilton frustrated by lack of Ferrari talks after Mexico clash
summary: Lewis Hamilton said on Thursday he remained frustrated by events at Ferrari during last week's Mexico City Grand Prix and had yet to hold any discussions about the opening-lap clash that wrecked their victory hopes.
Speaking in the Interlagos paddock ahead of this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix, the 41-year-old explained that team boss Fred Vasseur had returned to Italy between the races.
Sunday's race at Interlagos will be Hamilton's 400th Grand Prix.

stories.title: Talks with govt on petroleum levy in final stages: Jamaat-i-Islami
summary: ISLAMABAD: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) deputy chief Liaqat Baloch said on Thursday that negotiations with the government on the petroleum levy had reached their final stage, adding that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif bore the responsibility for making the talks successful.
During the meeting, JI experts briefed the party leadership on the progress of negotiations with the government.

Mr Baloch said all rounds of negotiations, as well as the meeting between the PM and JI chief, had established an understanding that the government would provide relief to consumers and gradually abolish what he described as an unjust tax.

stories.title: Turkish parliament approves Makkah defence pact with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia
summary: The Turkish parliament on Thursday approved a bill ratifying the Makkah Agreement on Joint Defence between Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, clearing the way for the trilateral security pact to take effect.

For Islamabad, the role also provides an opportunity to shape the working structure of the new defence arrangement as Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye move from the political commitment announced in Makkah towards a more organised mechanism for defence coordination.
The MJDA was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

stories.title: Arab countries condemn Houthi attempt to target Saudi Arabia’s Madinah region
summary: Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan on Thursday condemned an attempt by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi group to target Saudi Arabia’s Madinah region with a ballistic missile, reaffirming full solidarity with Riyadh.

In a statement, Jordan’s Foreign Ministry reaffirmed the country’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia, stressing its support for all measures taken by the kingdom to safeguard its security, stability, sovereignty and the safety of its citizens and residents.
The Saudi-led coalition said Thursday that its air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by Yemen’s Houthi militia toward the Madinah region.
